absent: Full layout of per CPU TLB state, flush info and batch structures and remote flush dispatch semantics.
Definition, default and upper bound of the single page flush threshold and debug directory lifetime.
Hardware invalidation primitive semantics and user identifier derivation from loaded state.
VMCS full layout, basic capability decoding, feature control meaning and trace hook behavior.
Complete encrypted virtualization configuration fields and hypervisor detection semantics.
Raw entry high word meaning, segment index and mapping macros, shift derivation and bookkeeping content.
Leaked secure page list structure, insertion paths and recovery behavior.
Memory mapping, allocation, CPU mask and online mask helper contracts used during setup.

findings.text: Single address invalidation always clears the kernel translation for the given address and, only when the PTI feature is enabled, also clears the user translation for the currently loaded address space, using a one entry INVPCID operation when that feature is present and the current processor has PCIDE enabled, and otherwise invalidating the whole user identifier.

Global invalidation prefers a single all context INVPCID operation whenever that feature is available regardless of PCIDE state, and otherwise performs a protected rewrite of the current CR4 value with interrupts saved and restored through raw primitives suitable for deep debugging contexts.

Local processor invalidation clears the user identifier for the currently loaded address space and then reloads the current page table base to discard local non global entries, requiring the caller to run with preemption disabled and tolerating a borrowed address space when the current task has none.

Batched unmap handling pins the current processor, then either performs a broadcast non global invalidation when the INVLPGB feature is present and unmapped pages are pending, or requests remote invalidation when other processors remain in the mask, or performs a local invalidation with interrupts briefly disabled when only the local processor is targeted, finally releasing the pin and clearing the mask.

A debug filesystem control for the single page flush threshold is registered at boot with read, write and seek handling, where read reports the current threshold as decimal text and write replaces it from user supplied decimal text.

Threshold updates propagate parsing failures to the caller, reject negative values with an invalid argument error, and otherwise store the new value and report full consumption of the supplied input, while reads only fail through the generic buffer helper.

Virtualization dispatch comprises a feature tag plus enable, disable and emergency disable callbacks held in a single global instance that becomes read only after initialization, alongside a globally visible rebooting flag that emergency paths set to indicate the system is going down.

Each processor tracks its own count of virtualization holders and shares one RCU protected emergency callback pointer, where registration warns and ignores a second registrant without overwriting, and unregistration warns on mismatch, clears the pointer and waits for readers before returning.

Acquisition validates that dispatch was initialized and that the requested feature matches the installed one, then under preemption protection increments the local holder count and invokes hardware enable only for the transition from zero to one, rolling the count back with a warning if enable fails.

Release runs under preemption protection, warns when no local holder exists, decrements the local count and returns early while holders remain, and otherwise invokes hardware disable and treats any failure as fatal unless the rebooting flag is already set.

Holder count lifecycle stays at zero with hardware disabled, moves to one with hardware enabled on first acquisition, remains enabled while nested acquisitions increment above one, and returns to disabled only when the last release decrements back to zero.

VMX support keeps one page sized root control structure per possible processor, allocated zeroed on the local node at init, stamped with the hardware reported revision identifier, used by physical address for entry, and freed with pointers cleared during cleanup on failure or dual technology conflict.

VMX enable rejects entry when extensions already appear active, records entry with the processor trace facility before attempting hardware entry and undoes that record on failure, while disable always clears the extension bit and trace state even when the hardware exit faults, reporting success or input output error accordingly.

SVM enable rejects entry when extensions already appear active and otherwise sets the extension bit, while disable first forces global interrupts enabled through a fault tolerant step and then clears the extension bit, preserving error status from the first step.

Emergency disable requires interrupts disabled, reports unsupported when no technology was installed, and otherwise invokes technology specific emergency handling that sets the rebooting flag, calls the registered guest callback when present and disables hardware if active; boot initialization probes both VMX and SVM, installs whichever succeeds, and disables everything with a warning if both unexpectedly succeed.

Global flush without hardware assist runs with raw interrupts saved, local batch flush briefly disables interrupts after asserting they were enabled, local single processor flush requires a non preemptible caller, holder count updates run under a preemption guard, and emergency disable asserts interrupts are already disabled.

The guest emergency callback is published with RCU assignment, removed with assignment plus a grace period wait, and read with a raw dereference in crash context to avoid lock checking, while leaked secure page accounting is serialized by a dedicated spinlock protecting its list and counter.

Firmware view reverse map entry holds a guest physical address, single bit assigned flag, single bit page size flag, single bit large page region status, single bit immutable flag, reserved bits and a thirty two bit address space identifier, with no compiler padding.

Raw reverse map entry is sixteen bytes viewed either as two sixty four bit words or as a bitfield with one bit each for assigned, size, immutable, save area, validated and one reserved top bit, nine reserved low bits, thirty nine bits of guest address and ten bits of identifier, with no padding.

Each address range descriptor stores a pointer to its entry array plus maximum index and byte size, with the top level table and its bound becoming read only after init and separate globals defining shift, coverage size and mask used to derive table position from physical address.
Firmware reserved bookkeeping area is sixteen kilobytes at the start of the reported region and the segmented table footprint read from firmware is four kilobytes.
Non segmented table shift is fifty two.
Second level page frame mask retains bits from second level granularity up to bit sixty three.
Segment table index bound starts at five hundred twelve entries.

Table establishment allocates a single zeroed page for top level pointers, then either validates one contiguous reservation covering all memory plus bookkeeping and self coverage with entries after the bookkeeping window, or walks firmware supplied segment records capping oversized mappings, deriving sixteen bytes per covered page, rejecting oversize segments, out of range indices and duplicate slots, requiring full RAM coverage while allowing extra high ranges for trusted IO, narrowing the bound to the highest used slot, mapping bookkeeping last and unwinding all mappings on any failure.

Secure nested paging preparation returns immediately when already active, otherwise clears reverse map state, requires every present processor to be online under the CPU read lock, flushes caches system wide, enables the memory type fixup bit and then the secure paging plus virtual privilege level bits on each processor, clears the save area pointer on each processor, and releases the lock with success or unsupported status.

Reverse map clearing does nothing without host secure paging support and warns without clearing when secure paging is already enabled, otherwise zeroes the per processor bookkeeping window and every installed segment.

Boot option parsing splits comma separated text, sets a debug flag when the debug token appears, clears host secure nested paging capabilities when the nosnp token appears outside a hypervisor and otherwise treats that token as unknown, and logs any unrecognized token while always reporting the option as handled.

Per processor helpers for memory fixup control, secure paging enable and save area clearing are invoked across all processors during preparation and each safely ignores processors without host secure paging support.

One entry invalidation with a nonzero identifier faults when PCIDE is clear so the current PCIDE state must be checked before use, global rewrite without hardware assist races preemption and interrupts without protection, and local reload requires disabled preemption to keep the page table base read and write on the same processor.

Entry faults report the feature control register and clear extensions, concurrent emergency calls may fault on control operations but are tolerated once rebooting is flagged, the crash callback read accepts a tiny unload race rather than taking locks, clearing reverse map state while secure paging is active would fault, and preparation fails when memory reservations or segment coverage are insufficient or when any processor is offline.
